flashcard_questions.q: Which term means the belief that government should not interfere in people's lives?
In which year did cholera first arrive in Britain?
Who published 'The Sanitary Conditions of the Labouring Population' in 1842?
What was the average life expectancy of a labourer in Manchester, according to that report?
The same report set a Manchester labourer's 17 years against what figure for a rural gentleman?
Which London water pump did John Snow link to the 1854 cholera outbreak?
What did John Snow's Soho investigation prove about cholera?
flashcard_questions.a: That it spread through contaminated water, not through bad air.

flashcard_questions.q: What was the key weakness of the 1848 Public Health Act?
flashcard_questions.a: It was not compulsory, so towns could ignore it.

flashcard_questions.q: Which 1858 event finally forced Parliament to pay for London's sewers?
Who was hired to design London's new sewer system?
How many miles of underground sewers did Bazalgette design?
Which law forced every council to appoint a Medical Officer of Health?
Pasteur published his Germ Theory in ____, explaining why filth spread disease.
Which 1867 Act gave the vote to many working-class men in towns?
In which year did Koch identify the bacterium that causes cholera?

notes: 15 cards: 5 event-to-date (one as cloze), 4 person-to-significance, 3 figure, 2 cause-effect, 1 term. Dropped the city population figures to avoid interference with the life-expectancy pair.
